models_evaluated: LLM-based visit preparation agent (standard and concise variants)
minimally prompted control chatbot on the same LLM

links.outcome: Visit preparedness, comprehensive preparation, and satisfaction for agent versus control chatbot in randomized study
links.effect: Agent had 16.6% higher comprehensive preparation (67.2% vs 50.6%, P<0.05) and 16.8% higher patient-reported preparedness (73.8% vs 57.0%, P<0.01); outcomes were visit readiness, not clinical outcomes.
links.quote: The visit preparation agent significantly outperformed the control across blinded clinician evaluations and patient self-reports.

links.outcome: Patient satisfaction and experience with AI-enabled visit preparation measured by post-surveys
links.effect: Overall satisfaction 12.0% higher with agent (74.0% vs 62.0%, P<0.05); confidence in knowing what to ask 81.4% vs 67.1% (P<0.01), n=460.
links.quote: Patient post-surveys (n = 460) showed 16.8% higher visit preparedness (73.8% vs. 57.0%; P < 0.01), 14.3% higher confidence in knowing what to ask (81.4% vs. 67.1%; P < 0.01), and 12.0% higher overall satisfaction (74.0% vs. 62.0%; P < 0.05).

unlisted_practices: Structured, workflow-based LLM prompting (visit preparation agent) versus minimally prompted chatbot to improve patient visit readiness

screen.reason: Prospective randomized study in real users comparing a structured visit-preparation AI agent/prompting workflow against a baseline minimally prompted control chatbot on the same LLM.

primary.practice: structured workflow and prompt design versus minimally prompted LLM
